Hi Alyssa — thanks, and sorry for the short timeline. See inline answers below and attached artifacts (audit-log-sample-2026-02-14.jsonl, siem-integration-guide.pdf, redwood-logging-evidence-map-soc2.xlsx).

Summary (high level)
- Events captured (examples):
  * Admin console authentication (SSO success/failure, MFA events)
  * API key and service principal lifecycle (create, rotate, revoke)
  * IAM/role changes (assign/remove roles, group membership changes)
  * Model lifecycle (deployment, rollback, version pinning)
  * Configuration changes (routing policies, batching/quantization toggles)
  * Job/controller actions (autoscale events, capacity changes)
  * Data plane accesses flagged for auditing (export requests, data retention changes)
  * System errors and elevated privilege actions

- Data captured per event (logged fields): timestamp (UTC), actor (internal user/service id), actor_email, action_type, request_id, request_path, http_method, status_code, ip_address, user_agent, resource_id, change_summary, previous_value, new_value, model_version, region, tenant_id.
  * Note: we do NOT include full user-provided prompt contents or full request/response bodies in standard audit logs. Request/response payload capture is optional and must be explicitly enabled (and can be configured to redact PII).

- Retention policy:
  * Default retention for audit logs: 13 months (395 days) in primary storage (meets typical SOC 2 evidence windows).
  * Longer-term aggregated metrics: 24 months (stored as metrics/rollups).
  * Retention start: event timestamp (UTC) recorded at ingestion; retention is windowed from ingestion time.

- Integrity and tamper controls:
  * Logs are written to an append-only backing store with server-side encryption (AES-256) and access logging.
  * Exported log bundles are signed with an HMAC-SHA256 signature; stored bundles include a signature manifest.
  * Internal change-history (who accessed/downloaded export) is also audited.

- Access control & export governance:
  * RBAC: only users with the Logging/Admin or Security role can view raw audit logs in the Console. Exports require elevated Export permission and are recorded.
  * Exports can be time-bounded, tenant-scoped, and filtered by event types.

- Export/integration options:
  * Direct S3 export (scheduled or on-demand): JSON Lines (jsonl) gzip bundles. Supports specifying prefix/date partitioning and cross-account role assumption.
  * Syslog/CEF over TLS: push to customer collector (IP + client cert).
  * SIEM integration: HTTP Event Collector (HEC) for Splunk or generic HTTPS ingestion endpoints — see attached siem-integration-guide.pdf for canonical config and sample curl commands.
  * API: /v1/admin/logs/export endpoint (token-scoped) that returns JSONL slices; supports filters (start_ts, end_ts, event_types, tenant_id). Rate-limited; recommended for incremental sync.
  * SFTP delivery: supported via managed outbound transfer (we can stage a signed bundle and deliver to an SFTP endpoint).

- Format & sample: attached audit-log-sample-2026-02-14.jsonl (anonymized): one JSON object per line; fields match the schema above. Bundles are compressed and accompanied by a signature manifest.

- PII/redaction:
  * By default, request/response payloads are not included; when enabled, payload capture supports field-level redaction rules and hashing.

- Mapping to SOC 2 logging controls: see attached redwood-logging-evidence-map-soc2.xlsx — the spreadsheet maps our logging features to common SOC 2 criteria (CC6.1, CC7.x style control IDs used by many auditors).

Next steps / options for FintechCorp
- Quick option: enable scheduled S3 export (daily) to your audit bucket; we can provide an ARN and a short-run test bundle within 24 hours.
- If you prefer SIEM push, provide your HEC endpoint + token and we’ll configure a test stream.
- If the auditor needs raw payloads for a short period, we can enable request capture for a scoped tenant and provide a signed bundle; this is manual and logged.

I’ve uploaded the three artifacts to the shared Drive and opened SEC-4231 for any follow-ups. If you want a short walkthrough for the auditor, Sean can run a 20-minute demo showing the export flow and signature verification.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
